title: LOW-IMPACT VELOCITY TOOLS FOR VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION OF CLOSE PROXIMITY OPERATIONS STRATEGIES EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a comprehensive set of rigorously tested tools that ensures monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance for close proximity operations.Description: Past activities related to Close Proximity Operations (CPO) highlighted the need ofdeveloping low impact velocity tools that can verify and validate that the servicer spacecraft (SC) maintains a collision risk probability of less than given threshold (e.g 10^-4) with the client SC during CPO. For missions involving multiple SC in close formation, the design of manoeuvres to avoid collisions with catalogue objects not belonging to the formation requires to take into account all SC of the formation, e.g. an avoidance manoeuvre performed by one SC of the formation shall not trigger an inner-formation collision risk but rather minimise disturbance to the formation while ensuring the required risk reduction. This activity aims at developing a comprehensive set of tools (e.g. DRAMA like tool, prototype software for formation flying) that ensure monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance during close proximity operations (including formation flying). This activity encompasses the followingtasks: - Develop and refine software tools that model the trajectory of both the target and servicer. - Develop algorithms that identify safe trajectories for close approaches and include collision avoidance features. - Develop tools that perform uncertainty propagation to estimate the likelihood of a collision between the servicer and client. - Identify sensor systems capable of providing design and operational level data about the relative positions, velocities, and orientations of both the servicer and the target. - Conduct virtual testing within the developed tools to simulate close approach and rendezvous operations in various scenarios. - Develop mathematical models of constraints and requirements and prototype a software solution suitable for realistic scenarios.

title: Finland – Rescue vessels – Market Dialogue notice: Kymenlaakso Rescue Department – DIGIMARIS Project_Oil Spill Response Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) for Coastal Operations
description: Background Kymenlaakso Rescue Department (KRD) is preparing the possible acquisition of an Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) for operational oil spill response in coastal and archipelago environments. The preparation is carried out within the DIGIMARIS project funded by the Interreg Central Baltic Programme. The purpose of this market dialogue is to improve the Contracting Authority's understanding of available technologies, integration approaches, operational limitations, delivery models, costs and life-cycle implications before launching a possible procurement procedure. KRD has not yet finalised the technical or commercial requirements for the potential future USV procurement. Suppliers and other market operators are therefore invited to provide information and comments on feasible operational performance, sensor integration, communication solutions, navigation and autonomy, maintenance concepts, information and cyber security, training, life-cycle services and other relevant aspects. KRD is particularly interested in understanding what can realistically be achieved with commercially available USV technology in coastal oil spill response operations and in Baltic Sea coastal and archipelago conditions. This notice constitutes a technical market dialogue and is not a call for tenders or a contract notice. The response is not a tender and does not bind the Contracting Authority or the respondent in any subsequent procurement procedure. The Contracting Authority is not obliged to proceed with the procurement. Information obtained through the market dialogue may be used in the preparation of a possible future procurement procedure. Operational Need The potential future USV is intended primarily for operational oil spill response. All other capabilities shall be considered supportive or optional unless otherwise specified. The potential future USV is expected to support the following tasks: • detection and monitoring of oil spills • provision of real-time situational awareness for incident command • operation in coastal and archipelago waters • remote operation from a vessel, shore or command centre • autonomous navigation along a predefined route • safe navigation and mission continuity during GNSS interference, spoofing or complete loss of the GNSS signal • hazardous gas assessment before rescue personnel approach the incident area • optional support for environmental monitoring and water rescue operations • optional deployment of containment booms or integration of other oil spill response equipment The Contracting Authority is seeking information on complete solutions as well as relevant platforms, payloads, sensors, software, integrations and life-cycle services. Respondents may propose a complete solution or identify the parts of the solution that they are able to provide. Market Dialogue Response Respondents shall complete the attached DIGIMARIS USV Technical Market Dialogue Response Workbook. The completed workbook and any supporting attachments shall be submitted in English through the Supplier Portal by the stated deadline. The respondent shall be responsible for all costs related to the preparation and submission of its response. The Contracting Authority may request clarifications concerning the information submitted. Any requests for clarification or further dialogue will be conducted in a transparent and non-discriminatory manner. Demonstrations and Trials KRD may invite respondents to present their solutions and, where feasible, to participate in operational demonstrations or trials in Finland. Demonstrations may include remote operation, autonomous navigation, oil detection, gas monitoring, situational awareness and operation in communications or GNSS-degraded conditions. Participation in demonstrations or trials will not provide an advantage in any possible future procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid for participation unless otherwise agreed separately in writing. Participation in the market dialogue, a presentation, demonstration or trial does not constitute a prerequisite for participation in any possible future procurement procedure.

description: Im Südwesten Berlins wird auf dem Gelände des dort in Betrieb befindlichen Umspannwerks Claszeile (Claszeile 55, 14165 Berlin-Zehlendorf) das vorhandene Umspannwerksgebäude erweitert und die Elektrotechnik erneuert. Die Ausschreibung und Vergabe des Projektes erfolgt in separaten Losen: Los 1: Baufeldfreimachung; Los 2: Baugrube und Gründung; Los 3: Hochbau Gebäude (inkl. Erdung, Blitzschutz, Brückenkran, TGA (ohne ELT)); Los 4: 110-kV-GIS zzgl. Feldverkabelung und Bedienschränke; Los 5: Elektrische Anlagen („GU-Los“). Diese Auftragsbekanntmachung bezieht sich ausschließlich auf das gegenständliche Los 5, Elektrische Anlagen bestehend u.a. aus: Errichtung einer 10-kV-Schaltanlage (2500A Bemessungsstrom und mit 74 Schaltfeldern), Errichtung der Leittechnik, Schutztechnik, Eigenbedarf, Nebenanlagen, die sekundärtechnische Anbindung der Transformatoren und Sternpunktbildner ab Zwischenklemmenkasten. Alle Schutzrelais werden vom Auftraggeber beigestellt. Zum Leistungsumfang des Los 5 gehören ferner die betriebsfertigen Verbindungen aller sekundären und primären Schnittstellen im Umspannwerk, die Prüfung, Inbetriebnahme, Dokumentation und die Anpassung der Schutz -und Leittechnik in den Gegenwerken und dem Servicearbeitsplatz, die Gesamtprojektsteuerung, Planung, Konstruktion, Fertigung, Werksprüfung (Systemtest Stationsleittechnik), Lieferung, Montage, Prüfung, Inbetriebnahme, Probebetrieb Gesamtsystem, Abnahme und Dokumentation, außer den bereits in Los 4 enthaltenen Leistungen. Der Auftragnehmer Los 5 muss mit den anderen Auftragnehmern, insbesondere Los 4, partnerschaftlich zusammenarbeiten um den angestrebten, qualitäts- und termingerechten Projekterfolg zu realisieren. Die Koordinationspflicht zur Wahrung der Auftraggeber-Interessen im Projekt UW CLZ obliegt dem Auftragnehmer Los 5, der Auftragnehmer Los 4 hat diesbezüglich eine Mitwirkungspflicht. title: 81321663-Provision of consultancy services for Long-Term Energy Planning and Renewable Energy Grid Integration
description: Under the GIZ initiative GET.transform, the contractor will support partner countries and regions in advancing the global energy transition through technical assistance and advisory services. The focus areas are Long-Term Energy Planning (LTEP) and Renewable Energy Grid Integration (REGI). The contractor will provide expert services, ensure flexibility to adapt to evolving needs, and contribute to achieving the overall programme objectives. GIZ will manage implementation jointly with local partners (worldwide), with English as the main working language, although other languages may be required depending on the project context. Regular coordination formats-such as weekly meetings and interim reports-will be established at the start of the assignment. Specific activities and expert assignments will be defined progressively based on partner requests. Objectives and Expected Results The contractor will strengthen the technical and institutional capacities of partner countries in energy planning and renewable energy integration. These areas are interconnected: sound energy planning must include strategies for renewable integration to ensure stability, affordability, and sustainability of electricity supply. 1. Long-Term Energy Planning Objective and Scope The goal is to improve the quality and effectiveness of long-term energy and power system expansion planning to support low-carbon and sustainable development. Approach Effective energy planning rests on three main pillars: - Governance and Consultation: Establish clear mandates, responsibilities, and coordination structures to guide planning exercises and ensure stakeholder participation. - Scenarios and Modelling: Develop data-driven, participatory modelling scenarios that reflect national development goals such as decarbonization, access to energy, economic growth, and equity. Reliable data management and transparency are essential to achieving credible outcomes. - Adoption and Communication: Ensure the outputs of planning and modelling are clearly communicated to policymakers, investors, and the public through implementation plans that outline steps, responsibilities, and timelines. The contractor should promote national ownership and capacity building by involving local experts and institutions in the process. Whenever possible, the use of open, transparent modelling approaches and accessible software tools is encouraged to strengthen local skills and ensure long-term sustainability. In some countries, particularly in Africa, the work may include integrated electrification planning aligned with national energy and development strategies. Geographic information systems (GIS) may be used to identify suitable sites for generation, transmission, and grid expansion. 2. Renewable Energy Grid Integration Objective and Scope The contractor will help partner countries (worldwide) enhance their ability to integrate higher shares of renewable energy into their power systems. This includes both technical planning and operational improvements necessary for reliable and efficient system transformation. Approach Partner countries face diverse challenges in integrating variable renewable energy sources such as solar and wind. Support activities may include: - Reviewing and updating grid codes, operational procedures, and compliance mechanisms. - Strengthening forecasting methods, grid flexibility measures, and stability analyses. - Developing transmission upgrade plans, energy storage strategies, and sector coupling solutions. - Building institutional and technical capacities through peer exchanges and training activities. All interventions will be tailored to each country"s stage in its energy transition and its broader development objectives. Collaboration and Adaptability The contractor must maintain a flexible and responsive working approach, adapting activities and work plans to changing needs and partner requests. A collaborative management system with GIZ will ensure regular communication, alignment on priorities, and continuous quality assurance. Deliverables Deliverables may include analytical studies, modelling exercises, policy and technical recommendations, capacity-building sessions, and communication materials. All outputs will be reviewed and approved by GIZ and its partners before completion. In summary, the contractor will act as a technical partner to GIZ, providing adaptable and high-quality support in energy planning and renewable grid integration. Through collaborative and capacity-oriented implementation, the work will help partner countries design integrated, sustainable, and low-carbon energy systems while fostering transparency, knowledge sharing, and long-term national ownership.
